high.title: Economists Raise Inflation for 2026; See This Monday's (11th) Focus Report
high.summary: Economists surveyed by the Central Bank adjusted their inflation projections for the ninth consecutive time, according to the Focus Bulletin released Monday morning. IPCA expectations for 2026 increased from 4.89% to 4.91%, exceeding the Central Bank's inflation target tolerance band. For 2027-2029, estimates remained at 4%, 3.64%, and 3.50% respectively. Selic rate forecasts stayed at 13% for this year, while 2027 projections rose to 11.25%. USD/BRL forecasts point to R$5.20 by year-end 2026, with subsequent years at R$5.30, R$5.35, and R$5.40. GDP growth is expected at 1.85% for 2026. This persistent upward revision in inflation expectations signals continued pressure on BCB monetary policy, suggesting the current restrictive stance may need to be maintained longer than previously anticipated. The breach of the inflation target tolerance band reinforces concerns about Brazil's fiscal sustainability and its impact on price stability, which could keep BRL under pressure and government bond yields elevated.

high.title: New Desenrola: How High Interest Rates Pressure Household Debt? Check It Out
high.summary: Economists assess that Brazil's elevated Selic rate combined with high banking spreads have contributed to increased household debt, prompting the government to launch the new "Desenrola" debt relief program. Banking spreads reached 34.6 percentage points in March versus 29.7 p.p. in March 2025, compared to the World Bank's global average of around 6 p.p. This elevated cost of credit directly impacts household finances and economic activity, highlighting the transmission mechanism of BCB's restrictive monetary policy on the real economy and creating fiscal pressures that may influence future rate decisions.

medium.title: Compass Debuts Today on B3, First IPO in Five Years; At Start, Potential Reaches 57%, Says Analyst
medium.summary: Compass, a gas distribution company from Cosan group, breaks Brazil's four-year IPO drought with its B3 debut. The company priced its offering at R$28, at the bottom of the range, raising R$3.2 billion and achieving a R$20 billion valuation. While pricing at the floor reflects weak market conditions amid Iran war uncertainties, EQI analysts see potential upside to R$42-44, representing up to 57% gains. This marks a significant milestone for Brazilian capital markets.
